page: Vultr vx1-g-16c-64g is a general-purpose server instance belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical AMD EPYC cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The processor includes 32 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1d cache. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is network-based with a local capacity of 1 GB, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark evaluations indicate top-tier single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core scoring 3621.68 and single-threaded gzip compression reaching 39.49 GB/sec. Text processing workloads also perform in the top 10%, scoring 3101.0 in Geekbench. Multi-core performance is average, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 28919.9 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 11731.0. Memory performance is strong, as reflected in the PassMark memory score of 2813.72, though uncached large-block memory bandwidth remains average at 88.72 GB/sec for reads and 45.8 GB/sec for writes. Small-model LLM text generation using a 135M model is highly efficient at 418.37 tokens/sec, while medium-model text generation operates at an average rate of 24.71 tokens/sec.

The instance offers a balanced resource profile suitable for general-purpose workloads, including web serving, software compilation, and database operations. The dedicated AMD EPYC cores provide consistent compute performance, though the 1 GB network-attached local storage capacity necessitates external storage solutions for data-heavy applications. The server is well-suited for text processing, single-threaded compression tasks, and lightweight language model inference, but is not designed for heavy multi-threaded compute or GPU-accelerated workloads.
